Rashi on Shabbat 52a:10:1.hebrew: כרוכין לימשך - כרוכים בריוח, שיכול להכניס ידו בין הכרך לצואר; או יניח מעט מן החבל, שאם באת לברוח, ימהר ויאחזנה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:10:1.english: Wrapped to be pulled - [They are] wrapped loosely, so that he can insert his hand between the wrapping and the neck; or he leaves a little of the rope, so that if [the animal] begins to run away, he can quickly seize it.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:13:1.hebrew: דאי ס"ד דרב דימי נמשכין לחוד קאמר - אבל כרוכין לא, ולא אתא לאשמעינן אלא דמולאות משתמרות באפסר, ולא הוי משוי להו:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:13:1.english: For if it would enter your mind that Rav Dimi said [they are] pulled alone - but wrapped, not [so]; and he only came to teach us that mules are guarded with a halter, and it is not a burden for them.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:13:2.hebrew: מדרב יהודה אמר שמואל נפקא - דקס"ד דקיבלה רבי מיניה דרבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:13:2.english: It is derived from [that which] Rav Yehuda said [that] Shmuel said - For it would enter one's mind that Rabbi accepted it from Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:17:1.english: A ring of a person - That one places on a finger for adornment.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:17:2.hebrew: טמאה - דתכשיט הוא, וממדין ילפינן, דמנה בהן תכשיטין — "אצעדה וצמיד" וגו', ואכולהו קאי: "תתחטאו אתם ושביכם" (במדבר לא):
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:17:2.english: Is ritually impure - For it is an ornament, and we learn [this] from Midian, where [the verse] enumerated ornaments among them: "An armlet and a bracelet," etc., and [the command] "Purify yourselves, you and your captives" (Numbers 31) applies to all of them.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:17:3.english: A ring of an animal - Such as a collar [shir].

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:17:4.english: A ring of utensils - Like that which they make at the top of the handles of utensils.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:17:5.english: And all other rings - Such as those made for a door:

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:1:1.english: That his mind would be eased - To inform him that I did not intend [to pass ahead of him].

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:1:2.hebrew: בפרומביא - מי הוי נטירותא יתירתא לגביה, או לא:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:1:2.english: With a halter - Is it [considered] excessive guarding for it, or not?

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:1:3.english: The halakha is in accordance with Chananya - And we do not care if it is excessive protection.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:2:1.hebrew: יוצאה באפסר - אם תחבו בחקיקת קרן, אבל בקשירה בעלמא — לא, דילמא שלפא מרישה, מתוך שראשה דק והיא מתנתקת לכאן ולכאן כשמושכין אותה, ואתי לאתויי ארבע אמות ברשות הרבים:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:2:1.english: May go out with a halter - [Only] if he inserted it into the carved hole of the horn; but with mere tying — [it may] not, lest it slip off its head, since its head is narrow and it twists from side to side when they pull it, and [the owner] will come to carry it four cubits in the public domain.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:2:2.hebrew: תחב לה בזקנה - שקשר שער זקנה כמין נקב, ותחב האפסר לתוכו:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:2:2.english: Inserted [it] into its beard - That he tied the hair of its beard in the form of a hole, and inserted the halter into it.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:2:3.english: Tears away - [It] tears itself away and leaps hither and thither to flee from his hand.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:2:4.hebrew: כאיב לה - הזקן, שנתלש השער ומכאיבה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:2:4.english: It hurts it - The beard, as the hair is pulled out and causes it pain.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:3:1.hebrew: תנן התם - בסוף פרקין: ולא פרה ברצועה שבין קרניה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:3:1.english: We learned there - At the end of our chapter: “Nor [may] a cow [go out] with a strap between its horns.”

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:3:2.hebrew: לנוי - שצובעה וקולעה לנוי בין קרניה, כמין קליעה מקרן לקרן, ואינו אוחזה בה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:3:2.english: For beauty - That he dyes it and braids it for ornament between its horns, like a kind of braid from horn to horn, and he does not hold [the cow] by it.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:3:3.english: To secure [it] - That he holds [the cow] by it.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:3:4.hebrew: אסור - דפרה מינטרא בלא אחיזה, אלא מוליכה לפניו. וקסבר: נטירותא יתירתא משוי הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:3:4.english: [It is] prohibited - For a cow is guarded without holding [it]; rather, one leads it before him. And he holds that excessive guarding is a burden.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:3:5.english: And to secure [it], it is permitted - He holds [that] extra guarding is not a burden.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:5:1.hebrew: ארבע בהמות - וקס"ד דהכי קאמר: באפסר יוצאו' ולא בחטם, אלמא נטירותא יתירתא משוי הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:5:1.english: Four animals - And it entered [our] mind that this is what he is saying: With a halter they may go out, but not with a nose ring; evidently, excessive guarding is a burden.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:6:1.hebrew: ומאי חזית - דמסמית הא דשמואל מקמיה ההיא? סמי ההיא מקמי הא:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:6:1.english: And what did you see - That you delete this [statement] of Shmuel on account of that [one]? Delete that [one] on account of this [one].

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:6:2.hebrew: דאיתמר - בהדיא דשמואל הוא דשרי. וההוא דמחליפין — כדאוקימנא: דלא למעוטינהו מחטם, אלא למעוטי נאקה מאפסר, דלא מינטרא ביה:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:6:2.english: As it was stated - [It is stated] explicitly that it is Shmuel who permits [it]. And that [tradition of] "they exchanged" [is interpreted] as we established: not to exclude them from [going out with] a nose ring, but to exclude a female camel from [going out with] a halter, as it is not secured by it.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:7:1.english: Its owner tied it - [Referring to] a red heifer:

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:7:2.english: With a halter [moseira] - [That is,] a halter [afsar].

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:8:1.hebrew: במוליכה מעיר לעיר - וסתם פרה פונה למקום מרבץ שלה, וצריך לאוחזה כשמוליכה לעיר אחרת; ולאו נטירותא יתירתא הוא, אלא אורחא היא:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:8:1.english: In [a case where] he is leading it from city to city - And an ordinary cow turns toward its resting place, and one must hold it when leading it to another city; and [so] it is not excessive guarding, but rather it is the normal practice.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:8:3.english: Whose value is high - And it requires extra guarding from [the time] it was born.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:9:1.hebrew: יוצאין כרוכין - הרצועה סביב צוארן, ואע"פ שאינו אוחזה — לאו משוי הוא, דלנוי נמי אורחייהו הוא:
Rashi on Shabbat 52a:9:1.english: They may go out wrapped - The strap [is wound] around their necks, and even though he is not holding it, it is not a burden, as it is also their normal practice [to wear it] for ornament.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:9:2.english: May be pulled - That [one] pulls it by the strap affixed to the ring of the chain.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:9:3.english: They may go out pulled - For safeguarding is the normal way.

Rashi on Shabbat 52a:9:4.english: And they may not go out wrapped - For [wearing it] as an ornament is not the usual way.

Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:10:1.hebrew: במתניתא תנא כרוכין לימשך - רב הונא מתרץ: כרוכים לימשך — שיש חלל בין אפסר לצואר, שהוא נוח לימשך כשירצה; ושמואל סבר: לימשך דוקא — שיש חבל תלוי באפסר:
Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:10:1.english: It was taught in a baraita: [They may go out] wrapped, to be pulled - Rav Huna explains [the phrase] "wrapped, to be pulled": that there is space between the halter and the neck, so that it is easy to be pulled when one wishes; and Shmuel holds: specifically "to be pulled" — that there is a rope hanging from the halter.

Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:17:1.hebrew: ומזין עליהם במקומן - אצטריך לאשמעינן במקומן, דלא חיישינן שמא תפול הזאה על הבהמה ויפסלו; דתנן במסכת פרה (סי"ב מ"ג): "נתכוון להזות על האדם והזה על הבהמה, אם יש באזוב — [לא] ישנה":
Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:17:1.english: "And one may sprinkle on them in their place" - It was necessary [for the Mishnah] to teach us "in their place," that we do not fear lest the sprinkling fall upon the animal and [the waters] become disqualified; as we learned in a mishna in tractate Parah (12:3): "[If] one intended to sprinkle upon a person and he sprinkled upon an animal, if [water] remains on the hyssop, he may [not] sprinkle again."

Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:17:2.hebrew: וטובלי' במקומן - הקשה הר"ר אליעזר: אמאי לא מקשה הכא "טבילה מאן דכר שמיה", כדפריך בריש "במה אשה" (דף נז.) אמאי דתנן "ולא תטבול עד שתרפם"? ותירץ ר"ת: דהכא לא פריך, משום דמתני' מיירי בדין כלים — שמחלק בין כלי לכלי, ואיזה מותר לצאת בו ואיזה אסור — ואגב אורחיה אשמעינן שאר דיני כלים: "ומזין עליהם וטובלן במקומן", דכן דרך התנא, כי ההוא (לקמן דף סו.): "דקיטע יוצא בקב שלו, ואם יש בו בית קבול כתותין טמא". אבל בריש "במה אשה", דמיירי בדיני כלים ואשמעינן דין טבילת אשה — פריך שפיר: "טבילה מאן דכר שמיה":
Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:17:2.english: "And immerse them in their place" - Harav Rabbi Eliezer raised a difficulty: Why does [the Gemara] not ask here, "Who mentioned anything about immersion?" — as it asks at the beginning of [the chapter] Bameh Ishah (57a) regarding that which we learned: "and she may not immerse [while wearing] them until she loosens them"? And Rabbeinu Tam answered: Here [the Gemara] does not ask [this], because our Mishnah deals with the laws of utensils — distinguishing between [one] utensil and [another] utensil, and which one it is permitted [for an animal] to go out with and which one is forbidden — and in passing, it teaches us other laws of utensils: "and one may sprinkle upon them and immerse them in their place," for such is the way of the Tanna, like that [Mishnah] (below, 66a): "An amputee may go out with his wooden leg... and if it has a receptacle for pads, it is ritually impure." But at the beginning of Bameh Ishah, where [the Mishnah] deals with the laws of utensils and [yet] teaches us the law of a woman's immersion, [the Gemara] rightly asks: "Who mentioned anything about immersion?"

Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:1:1.hebrew: אמר שמואל הלכה כחנניא - פר"ח דהלכה כרב, דאמר: בין לנוי בין לשמר — אסור, מדמשני אביי ורבא ורבינא, דהוו בתראי, אליביה ההיא דקשרה בעליה במוסרה. ועוד, דקיי"ל דהלכתא כרב באיסורי. הלכך אומר הרב פור"ת, דכל נטירותא יתירתא אסור, כגון פרה באפסר; ובכל נוי בהמה אסור לצאת. ומיהו עגלים יוצאות באפסר, כדאמר בסמוך; ויוצא סוס ברסן, דאורחיה בהכי, או באפסר, אבל בשניהם, ברסן ובאפסר — אסור. ומותר להשים הרסן או האפסר בראש הסוס בשבת, ואין בו איסור טלטול, דמוכן הוא לבהמה. ואדם המנהיג סוס ברשות הרבים, יזהר שלא יוציא ראש החבל מתחת ידו טפח, ומה שבין ידו לסוס יגביה מן הקרקע טפח, דהכי אמרינן לקמן בפרקין. ומותר לכרוך חבל האפסר סביב צואר הבהמה ולצאת, דהא עגלי דרב הונא ומולאות של בית רבי יוצאים כרוכין:
Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:1:1.english: Shmuel said: The halakha is in accordance with Ḥananya - Rabbeinu Ḥananel explained that the halakha is in accordance with Rav, who said that whether [it is worn] for ornamentation or for restraint, it is forbidden — since Abaye, Rava, and Ravina, who were the later [Amoraim], answered according to his view [the challenge from] that [baraita of] 'its owner tied it with a halter.' And furthermore, we maintain that the halakha follows Rav in [matters of ritual] prohibitions. Therefore, Rabbi Porat says that any excessive restraint is forbidden, such as a cow [going out] with a halter; and with any animal ornamentation, it is forbidden to go out. However, calves may go out with a halter, as [the Gemara] states nearby; and a horse may go out with a bridle, for that is its typical manner, or with a halter, but with both of them — with a bridle and with a halter — it is forbidden. And it is permitted to place the bridle or the halter on the head of the horse on Shabbat, and there is no prohibition of handling [it], for it is designated for the animal. And a person who leads a horse in the public domain must take care that he does not let the end of the rope protrude from beneath his hand by a handbreadth, and that which is between his hand and the horse he must raise a handbreadth above the ground, for so we say later in our chapter. And it is permitted to wind the halter rope around the animal's neck and go out, for behold, the calves of Rav Huna and the mules of the House of Rabbi would go out wound [with ropes].

Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:5:1.hebrew: אדרבה תסתיים דשמואל הוא דאמר כו' - תימה לרשב"א: מה ראייה מייתי מדאמר שמואל "מחליפין לפני רבי כו'"? דלכאורה משמע דהא דקאמר לעיל "לא, למעוטי נאקה באפסר" — דכל זה מדברי שמואל:
Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:5:1.english: "On the contrary, conclude that Shmuel is the one who said, etc." - It is astonishing to the Rashba: What proof does [Abaye] bring from that which Shmuel said, "They exchanged before Rabbi, etc."? For seemingly it implies that that which [the Gemara] said above, "No, to exclude a female camel with a halter" — that all of this is from the words of Shmuel.

Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:7:1.hebrew: קשרה בעליה במוסרה - הוה מצי לשנויי: הא מני? חנניא היא. והא דמשמע בריש הכונס (ב"ק נה:) דמוסרה שמירה פחותה היא — היינו דוקא בשור:
Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:7:1.english: "If its owner tied it with a halter" - [The Gemara] could have answered: Whom does this [baraita] follow? It is Hananiah [who maintains that excessive guarding is not considered a burden]. And [as for] that which is implied at the beginning of HaKones (Bava Kamma 55b), that a halter is [merely] minimal guarding — that is specifically regarding an ox.

Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:9:1.hebrew: או יוצאין כרוכין - פי' בקונט' דמכוין לנוי, וכן פירש במתניתין. וקשה לרשב"א ולהרב פור"ת, דלעיל משמע דלנוי לכ"ע אסור! ותירץ הרב פור"ת דבהא פליגי: דרב הונא סבר דנטירותא נמי איכא בכרוכין — שאם רוצה הבהמה לברוח יתפסנה בכריכת האפסר, ולא הוי משוי; ושמואל סבר: כרוכין לא הוי נטירותא:
Tosafot on Shabbat 52a:9:1.english: "Either they may go out wrapped" - The Kuntres [Rashi] explained that he intends [it] for ornamentation, and so he explained in the Mishnah. And the Rashba and the Rav Porat found this difficult, for above it implies that [going out] for ornamentation is forbidden according to everyone! And the Rav Porat answered that this is what they disagree about: Rav Huna holds that there is also [an element of] protection when [it is] wrapped, as if the animal wants to flee, one can seize it by the coil of the halter, and [therefore] it is not a burden; and Shmuel holds [that when] wrapped, it is not considered protection.
